name: subagent-model-router
description: Modified copy of an MIT-licensed Jev model router that uses Haiku in place of Jev. Haiku reads each subagent task at agent.spawn and answers in JSON with a tier and a confidence from 0 to 1; a task moves to a cheaper model only when that confidence is at least minDowngradeConfidence. Logs every pick, the model it replaced and the estimated cost difference to ~/.claude/mods-logs/savings.jsonl. No API key and no network call of its own. Never changes the main chat's model; main-chat effort routing is off by default.

fastModel.title: Fast tier
fastModel.description: Model alias or id for mechanical, local tasks

balancedModel.title: Balanced tier
balancedModel.description: Model alias or id for ordinary engineering work

deepModel.title: Deep tier
deepModel.description: Model alias or id for hard or high-stakes work

minUpgradeConfidence.title: Confidence to spend more
minUpgradeConfidence.description: How sure Haiku must be to raise the model or the effort; being wrong here costs money, so the bar is low

minDowngradeConfidence.title: Confidence to spend less
minDowngradeConfidence.description: How sure Haiku must be to lower the model or the effort; being wrong here means a task gets too little, so the bar is high. A missing or unreadable confidence never lowers anything

routeSubagentModel.title: Route subagent models
routeSubagentModel.description: Pick the model of each subagent at agent.spawn (the Agent tool takes no effort)

routeMainEffort.title: Route the main loop's effort
routeMainEffort.description: Raise or lower the reasoning effort of the main conversation. Off by default: a mid-chat effort change can throw the message cache away. Left alone while Stably is on for the turn

timeoutMs.title: Judge time limit (ms)
timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for Haiku's answer before letting the request through unchanged. Haiku takes about 1.3 s, so keep this well above that

logDecisions.title: Log decisions
logDecisions.description: Also show each routing decision in the session log (the file log and the ledger are always written)
